sec-head.p: A vector embedding is a list of numbers — a mathematical representation — that captures the meaning of a piece of text, an image, or any data. Instead of storing words like 'cat' and 'dog', a model converts them into points in space where similar meanings sit close together.

ul: The word 'king' becomes a vector like [0.2, 0.7, -0.1, 0.4, ...]
The word 'queen' becomes a vector like [0.3, 0.8, -0.2, 0.5, ...]
These two vectors are 'close' in the embedding space because their meanings are similar
A vector for 'apple' (fruit) sits near 'banana' but far from 'apple' (company)
A diagram would show three clusters: fruits, companies, and animals — each cluster grouping related meanings

step.body: A pre-trained embedding model, like OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small, takes your text and outputs a fixed-length vector — typically 256 to 1536 numbers.
Vectors live in a high-dimensional space. The distance between two vectors (cosine similarity) measures how similar their meanings are — closer means more related.
A vector database indexes these embeddings. At query time, it converts your question into a vector and finds the nearest neighbors — the most semantically relevant documents.
The system returns the original text chunks whose vectors are closest to the query vector, enabling accurate retrieval without exact keyword matching.

faq-item.faq-q: What exactly is a vector embedding?
faq-item.faq-a: A vector embedding is a list of numbers that represents the meaning of a piece of data — text, image, or audio — in a high-dimensional space. Similar meanings produce vectors that are close together, enabling semantic search.

faq-item.faq-q: How is an embedding different from a keyword?
faq-item.faq-a: A keyword is an exact word that must match literally. An embedding captures meaning, so 'car' and 'automobile' will have similar vectors even though they are different strings. This is why embeddings power semantic search.

faq-item.faq-q: How many numbers are in a typical vector?
faq-item.faq-a: Modern embedding models output vectors with 256 to 1536 dimensions — that is, 256 to 1536 numbers. Higher dimensions capture more nuance but increase storage and compute cost.

faq-item.faq-q: Can I create my own embedding model?
faq-item.faq-a: You can fine-tune an existing embedding model on your domain, but most applications use a pre-trained model from OpenAI, Cohere, or sentence-transformers. Fine-tuning is only needed for highly specialized vocabularies.

Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors; it ranges from -1 (opposite meaning) to 1 (identical meaning). It is the most common metric for comparing embeddings because it ignores vector length and focuses on direction.
